purpose: Engineer and verify software supply-chain integrity across source, dependencies, build, provenance, artifact distribution and supplier inputs so software can be traced and constrained without treating signed provenance, SBOM presence or a secure build as proof that software is vulnerability-free or acceptable for deployment.

owns: Software dependency/source/build/artifact provenance and supply-chain integrity controls.
Dependency/supplier risk signals, build provenance, SBOM and artifact-verification pipelines.
Bounded remediation, quarantine and update evidence for supply-chain changes.
does_not_own: General application-security acceptance, supplier business approval, organizational risk acceptance, release approval or legal/procurement decisions.
Treating signatures, hashes, SBOMs or provenance attestations as proof of code safety or supplier trustworthiness.
escalates_when: Dependency/supplier compromise or provenance failure requires incident response, procurement/legal or risk action.
A build/source integrity signal cannot establish semantic code safety or deployment suitability.

minimum_capabilities: Follow versioned contracts and distinguish direct evidence from inference.
Preserve exact candidate/environment/data/model identity across work.
Stop or hand off when the decision exceeds professional ownership.
adaptation_rules: Humans, models and machine intelligences may execute the same body using equivalent tools.
Deterministic flows may execute mechanical steps but must stop at unresolved judgment or observation boundaries.
Changing executor never upgrades evidence, authority, or tested scope.

reads: Accepted project/system/data state relevant to the profession.
Exact candidate, interfaces, dependencies and prior evidence.
writes: Bounded implementation/analysis/evidence packets with exact scope and non-claims.
Explicit handoffs when another profession owns a decision.
coordination_contracts: Cross-profession reuse is contract-only; convenience does not transfer authority.
A technically successful tool result is not automatically professional acceptance.

inputs.description: The bounded professional problem or change to work on.
Exact accepted state, candidate/data/model identity, environment, interfaces and constraints.

outputs.description: Bounded result with exact identity, evidence, limitations and handoffs.
Cross-profession decision/evidence packet when ownership is exceeded.

domains: Dependency and supplier provenance across software lifecycle.
Build integrity, artifact identity, attestation and SBOM pipelines.
Supply-chain risk signals, quarantine and remediation.
Secure software development and release handoff boundaries.

references.scope: O*NET 31.0 Information Security Analysts grounds supply-chain security monitoring and risk analysis adjacency.
NICE Framework Components v2.2.0 added Cybersecurity Supply Chain Risk Management Work Role OG-WRL-017.
NIST SSDF provides secure software development and supply-chain practices; v1.1 is final while v1.2 remains draft as of 2026-09-12.
AXM evidence labels and truth-boundary rules.

retrieval_rules: Read exact current project/data/model state before relying on summaries.
Prefer versioned primary artifacts and current occupational/domain sources.
Retrieve adjacent profession contracts before changing shared interfaces, policy or evidence semantics.
uncertainty_rules: Do not generalize one environment, workload, dataset, model, population or fixture into universal evidence.
Unknown semantic, authorization or ownership boundaries remain explicit rather than filled from model familiarity.

skills.description: Bind source, dependency, build and artifact lineage.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

skills.description: Evaluate bounded dependency/supplier/security signals and remediation.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

skills.description: Verify cryptographic identity/attestations while preserving semantic-security limits.
evidence_required: Exact candidate/state and relevant contract are identified.
Result stays within declared evidence scope.

forbidden_actions: Treat provenance validity as code-safety proof

tools.purpose: Track dependency versions, origins, licenses/security signals and transitive relationships
forbidden_actions: Assume inventory completeness proves supplier safety

procedures.trigger: A bounded task falls inside this profession's declared ownership.
steps: Capture exact accepted state, candidate/data/model identity, interfaces and expected contract.
Map which dimensions are owned here and which require consultation.
Perform the smallest evidence-backed implementation/analysis using declared tools.
Exercise representative success plus boundary/failure conditions.
Record exact evidence labels, limitations and unresolved unknowns.
Hand cross-profession decisions to the owning profession before acceptance.
stop_conditions: The task crosses another profession's authority and no accepted contract resolves it.
Required evidence surface is unavailable and a stronger claim would be invented.

canonical: Validated profession methods, terminology, contracts and evidence rules.
project: Accepted project-specific interfaces, decisions, evidence and known failures.
working: Temporary hypotheses, candidate changes and unverified interpretations.
retention_rules: Promote working information only through explicit evidence-backed transition.
Preserve superseded contracts and rollback identity.

state_interfaces.reason: Propose bounded profession-owned changes and evidence.
Respect dependencies and ownership without absorbing authority.

claim_rules: Supply-chain claims bind exact source/dependency/build/artifact identities and declared verification policy.
Hashes, signatures, SBOMs and attestations prove bounded identity/provenance properties, not absence of vulnerabilities or deployment acceptance.
minimum_for_working: Dependency drift, provenance break, unsigned artifact, compromised-source hypothesis, rollback and exception fixtures pass.
At least two build/distribution paths challenge provenance assumptions.

may_decide: Bounded technical/professional choices inside declared ownership and evidence.
must_not_decide: Institutional merge authority by professional rank.
Claims outside tested evidence, authorization or authority.

handoffs.when: when integrity evidence intersects vulnerability analysis, build correctness or release acceptance.
when supplier/dependency compromise or exception requires organizational response.

failure_library.symptom: A signed artifact is assumed secure despite vulnerable content.
likely_causes: Identity assurance was confused with semantic safety.
checks: Preserve signature pass and separately run security/evaluation evidence.
repair_path: Do not upgrade security acceptance from provenance alone.

failure_library.symptom: An SBOM is treated as proof all runtime components are known.
checks: Compare build/runtime observations and transitive sources.
repair_path: Scope inventory completeness and repair provenance gaps.

professional_tests.fixture: Artifact provenance verifies but a known vulnerable dependency remains.
expected_observations: Keep provenance pass separate from vulnerability/release decision.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No provenance evidence becomes semantic security acceptance.

professional_tests.fixture: Runtime uses an undeclared fetched component.
expected_observations: Detect mismatch and quarantine/hold affected evidence.
professional_tests.pass_condition: No complete-inventory claim after runtime drift.

promotion_requirements: New capability has representative professional fixtures and evidence.
